publicReleaseNotes: Penny 0.2.2 keeps the feedback page readable while a workspace export or backup holds the data lock. On RER Managed, Penny 0.2.1 answered most GET /app/feedback requests with an error while an export was open; operator reads now check the session without waiting for the lock, changes still pause until the export ends, and the pause notice shows only on the feedback page and clears when the export is finished or aborted. The release also carries main's work since 0.2.1: email capture to a dedicated address (CAP-009), requester Google and GitHub sign-in (REQ-039), owner-enabled sensitive-evidence rules (AI-008, partial), cited AI summaries and reply drafts (AI-006), weekly requester summaries (NOTIFY-010, partial), audited request tag and assignment batches with undo (TRIAGE-005, partial), roadmap links to published releases and hardening fixes. Migrations 0088 to 0095 are additive. It runs on rer 0.2.80 and carries the hosted installation descriptor, mail setup and retained source custody for listing. Backup compatibility changes: v2 archives without the schemaObjects inventory are refused; create a fresh export from the existing installation with rer 0.2.80 before relying on restore. Local setup and dev on a Platform-migrated database, SendGrid duplicate suppression, live external feedback providers, hosted email capture and social sign-in, the weekly digest mailbox receipt and whole-product acceptance beyond the proved core loop remain known limits. CAP-009.summary: Email capture ships against provider-edge fixtures: direct or BCC copies are attributed to the admitted sender, Message-ID digests survive erasure so a replay cannot recreate an item, refusals keep only non-personal counts and provenance reads "Forwarded by <admitted sender>"; hosted Email Routing and live mail are not yet run.
CAP-009.was: Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Operators forward or BCC customer emails to it. Penny accepts only mail from operator addresses or allowlisted domains with DMARC alignment, recovers the original sender from the forwarded message, keeps attachments within `seed.json` limits and creates one inbox item per message ID. Notification reply addresses never reach this route, and it refuses mail from Penny's own sender addresses (`MAIL_FROM` and any NOTIFY-013 sender), as NOTIFY-004 requires. *Acceptance:* Inbound-mail fixtures: forwarded Gmail and Outlook messages each create one item attributed to the original sender; a replayed message ID, an unaligned sender, mail from Penny's own sender address and a reply to a Penny notification create nothing.
CAP-009.now: Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Direct or BCC copies without recoverable forwarded headers are attributed to the admitted sender and marked not forwarded. Message-ID digests stay after erasure so a replay cannot recreate an item. Refusals keep only non-personal reason counts. Hosted Email Routing, a real domain and live mail acceptance: NOT RUN. Admission depends on the `Authentication-Results: mx.cloudflare.net;` header, which only a hosted receipt can confirm. HTML-only mail is refused (`excerpt_size_or_plain_text_required`). Captured source provenance records "Forwarded by <admitted sender>"; a recovered body address is labeled "Sender stated in forward".

AI-006.summary: Cited summaries and reply drafts ship: drafting reads only records the operator can open, unresolvable citations are dropped with a visible notice, a draft holding a private value is flagged and its publication refused until edited, nothing sends itself and a revoked session refuses a draft completed in flight.
AI-006.was: For a request, decision or account, Penny drafts a cited summary of its evidence and discussion; for comments and inbox items it drafts a reply or status-update wording that an operator edits and sends. Drafts never send themselves, and a draft carrying a private value (an account name, revenue, an internal note) is flagged before publication (EVID-006). *Acceptance:* Every citation in a fixture summary resolves to a stored record; a draft containing a private account name is flagged; nothing is sent without the operator's action.
AI-006.now: For a request, decision or account, Penny drafts a cited summary of its evidence and discussion; for comments and inbox items it drafts a reply or status-update wording that an operator edits and sends. Drafts never send themselves, and a draft carrying a private value (an account name, revenue, an internal note) is flagged before publication (EVID-006). Drafting reads only records available to the current operator; the prompt obeys AI-010’s data-processing setting. Unresolvable citations are dropped with a visible notice and never displayed as cited. Replies today are public request comments, posted only after the operator edits and posts; this draft feature sends no email or connector reply. Unlinked inbox drafts remain editable until linked to a published request. Future connector and mail replies under NOTIFY-007, CAP-003, CAP-004, CAP-005, CAP-006, CAP-019 and CAP-009 inherit the operator edits and sends, never auto-send, and a fresh private-value check before publication. AI-011 carries measured quality (none of its evaluation bars apply to this clause); ROLE-001 carries the missing restricted-commercial-field roles, including draft context and publication checks. These inherited obligations do not narrow the shipped drafting flow. *Acceptance:* Every citation in a fixture summary resolves to a stored record; unknown citations are dropped and disclosed; a draft containing a private account name is flagged and its publication refused until edited; nothing is sent without the operator's action. A revoked session refuses a draft completed in flight.

AI-008.summary: Deterministic rule-only redaction ships as partial: operator evidence, email capture and portal submissions are redacted before storage and an explicit reapplication covers at most 200 evidence versions; saved-import originals, learning source envelopes and model detection remain open.
AI-008.was: Owner-configured rules (US Social Security numbers, payment card numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, credential shapes and custom patterns), with optional model detection, redact captured excerpts and transcripts before storage; redactions are marked, and the unredacted original stays only in the source system. *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set redaction-v1` (AI-011) reports recall of at least 0.99 for Social Security and payment card numbers and at least 0.95 for the other default kinds, with precision of at least 0.90; a fixture ticket containing an SSN and a card number is stored redacted in D1, search and the archive; a new rule applies to new captures and, on request, re-applies to stored ones.

Binary attachments are not rewritten. Operator evidence, CAP-009 email capture and native portal submission use guarded before-storage rules. AI-011 remains missing and inherits extending the minimal redaction-v1 runner. Gap: saved-import originals and learning source envelopes are not redacted before storage. NOTIFY-013.summary: CAP-009 now proves the reciprocal capture-address exclusion; the remaining sender-identity settings stay open.
NOTIFY-013.was: Owners and Admins set, in settings, how requester and release email presents the business, as Canny's email whitelabeling does: the sender name (default: the INT-007 company name), the from address on a domain verified with the owner's mail provider (Penny sends a test message to the operator and shows the provider's result before saving, and refuses an address the provider rejects), an optional monitored reply-to address that is never the CAP-009 capture address (without one, replies go to the no-reply address under NOTIFY-004), and the business postal address. Every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, NOTIFY-008–NOTIFY-012, REL-005, REQ-030's rejection notice) uses the sender name and from address and carries the postal address in its footer with the one-click unsubscribe, as CAN-SPAM requires. First-run setup (OPS-005) asks for the postal address with the company name and cannot finish without both; an installation set up earlier shows its owner a one-time prompt alongside OPS-008's. Until a postal address is recorded, the paths that email people who did not ask in that moment cannot be turned on or chosen, each refused with the reason: vote subscriptions (NOTIFY-008), author subscriptions (NOTIFY-011), the captured-contact send (NOTIFY-009), the weekly digest (NOTIFY-010) and MIG-007 carry-over; boards created meanwhile start with vote subscriptions off; mail a requester explicitly asked for (a follow, an Email me updates tick, an updates subscription) still sends; and the overview shows the missing address until it is set. Operator email (NOTIFY-003, NOTIFY-006) uses the same from address and needs no postal address. migrations.buyerSteps: Adds email capture (CAP-009): the owner's capture address, the exact sender-domain allowlist, SHA-256 Message-ID digests with no item foreign key (so an erased item cannot be recreated by a replay) and non-personal refusal reason counts. New tables only; nothing is captured until the owner sets an address and routes it to the Worker's email handler.

Adds requester Google and GitHub sign-in (REQ-039): one switch per provider, off by default, and single-use sign-in states that expire after ten minutes. No credential or provider subject is stored; client credentials stay installation bindings. New tables only.
Adds sensitive-evidence rules (AI-008): one policy row with kinds, custom patterns and a revision, off by default. New table only; nothing is redacted until the owner enables rules.
Adds the nullable evidence_items.admitted_sender column for email-capture provenance. Existing evidence keeps NULL (unknown); never infer a forwarder from body wording. Keep the column on rollback.

Adds the weekly requester summary (NOTIFY-010): the owner switch (off until enabled), each requester's address-bound choice and live publication custody, under the data-maintenance guards. New tables and triggers only; nothing is sent until the owner enables it and a requester opts in.

Adds audited request tag and assignment batches (TRIAGE-005) with before and after snapshots for undo, under the data-maintenance guards. New tables and triggers only; a restored batch is history and never an actionable undo.

Adds keys_sealed (default 0) and key_ids (default '[]') to the rer_dependency_installation record, so a restored row can name an unavailable retired key without being mistaken for tampering or a wrong secret. Columns with defaults; no owner action.

Adds durable pages and content revision tracking for owner-authorized redaction runs. Existing rows and applied migration bytes are retained; unfinished executable redaction state stays local and is not portable.
